The #49 work that remains (owner-authorized `gdc ops site` / `gdc ops edge`, public inference acceptance, the DevShard v5 rollout, and the Gonka v0.2.16 transition) needs owner-held credentials and live infrastructure. This PR does not attempt any of it.\n\nPart of #49.\n\n## Defect and root cause\n\n`https://gonka-dev.net/status/gateway-health` currently reports values like `\"latency_ms\": 19651863` and `23603745` for a probe that runs every few seconds.\n\nThe OPS scripts took millisecond timestamps with `date +%s%3N`. Ubuntu 26.04, a supported Host OS, ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0 as `date`, and that `date` ignores the `%3N` width and prints unpadded nanoseconds:\n\n| `date` implementation | `date +%s%3N` |\n|---|---|\n| GNU coreutils 9.1 / 9.4 | `1790273287205` (correct) |\n| uutils 0.3.0 – 0.6.0 | 13 digits (correct) |\n| uutils 0.7.0 | `1790273355137920493` |\n| uutils 0.8.0 (stock `ubuntu:26.04` image) | `1790274278470608404` |\n| uutils 0.9.0 – 0.12.0 | 13 digits (correct) |\n\nThese values were checked on 2026-09-24 with the upstream uutils release binaries and the `ubuntu:26.04` container. Because the output is unpadded, the difference between two readings is in nanoseconds, or garbage when the digit counts differ. Fed the uutils-0.7 behaviour, the unmodified `main` probe published `latency_ms: -1611246130079893093`.\n\n## Change\n\n- Every `date +%s%3N` in `04-ops/` and `scripts/` becomes `$(( ${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/} / 1000 ))`, the bash ≥ 5.0 builtin. Bash 5.3 on Ubuntu 26.04 and bash 5.1/5.2 on 22.04/24.04 provide it, and these scripts already need bash 4 features (`declare -A`, `mapfile`). No `date` subprocess, no shared helper file, and nothing new for `install-ops.sh` to deploy. This replaces the two copies of `epoch-millis.sh` from the earlier revision.\n- The readiness waiter rejects a `completion_finished_ms` later than now + 1 s, so a probe host that still produces nanosecond receipts can't pass for fresh.\n- The public health schema checks in `verify-public-homepage.sh` and `capture-gateway-observability.sh` bound `latency_ms` to `[0, 60000]` and require a 13-digit `completion_finished_ms` when it isn't zero.\n\n`devnet/node_scripts/find_best_rpc.sh` also uses `%3N` but belongs to a different tree, so it is left unchanged here.\n\n## Tests\n\n- `scripts/test-gateway-health-probe.sh` runs the real probe with a `date` on `PATH` that behaves like uutils 0.7/0.8, and asserts `latency_ms` is in `[0, 60000]` and `completion_finished_ms` has 13 digits. It fails against the `main` probe and passes on this branch.\n- `scripts/test-public-traffic-readiness.sh` adds a nanosecond-scale future receipt, which must be rejected.\n- `scripts/test-profiles.sh` fails if any `$(date …%3N)` comes back into `04-ops/` or `scripts/`.\n- Locally, `make shellcheck` (ShellCheck v0.11.0) passes, and `GONKA_UPSTREAM_WORKTREE=<gonka clone> make test` passes except `test-recovery-contract`, which was skipped. In this environment it fails the same four assertions (`new persistent output accepted` and three that follow from it) on unmodified `main`.\n- CI for this fork PR still needs maintainer approval.\n\n## Deployment status\n\nNothing is deployed by this PR. The live probe keeps reporting nanosecond latencies until an owner-authorized OPS reinstall puts the updated `gateway-health-probe.sh` on the gateway Host.\n\n 12 files changed, 66 insertions(+), 31 deletions(-)",

[2026-09-24T18:45:32.069Z] [STDOUT] ## Scope

This PR is **not** a solution for issue #49. It fixes one defect found on the way: the public gateway health document reports wrong `latency_ms` values, and request deadlines use the wrong unit. The #49 work that remains (owner-authorized `gdc ops site` / `gdc ops edge`, public inference acceptance, the DevShard v5 rollout, and the Gonka v0.2.16 transition) needs owner-held credentials and live infrastructure. This PR does not attempt any of it.

Part of #49.

## Defect and root cause

`https://gonka-dev.net/status/gateway-health` currently reports values like `"latency_ms": 19651863` and `23603745` for a probe that runs every few seconds.

The OPS scripts took millisecond timestamps with `date +%s%3N`. Ubuntu 26.04, a supported Host OS, ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0 as `date`, and that `date` ignores the `%3N` width and prints unpadded nanoseconds:

| `date` implementation | `date +%s%3N` |
|---|---|
| GNU coreutils 9.1 / 9.4 | `1790273287205` (correct) |
| uutils 0.3.0 – 0.6.0 | 13 digits (correct) |
| uutils 0.7.0 | `1790273355137920493` |
| uutils 0.8.0 (stock `ubuntu:26.04` image) | `1790274278470608404` |
| uutils 0.9.0 – 0.12.0 | 13 digits (correct) |

These values were checked on 2026-09-24 with the upstream uutils release binaries and the `ubuntu:26.04` container. Because the output is unpadded, the difference between two readings is in nanoseconds, or garbage when the digit counts differ. Fed the uutils-0.7 behaviour, the unmodified `main` probe published `latency_ms: -1611246130079893093`.

## Change

- Every `date +%s%3N` in `04-ops/` and `scripts/` becomes `$(( ${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/} / 1000 ))`, the bash ≥ 5.0 builtin. Bash 5.3 on Ubuntu 26.04 and bash 5.1/5.2 on 22.04/24.04 provide it, and these scripts already need bash 4 features (`declare -A`, `mapfile`). No `date` subprocess, no shared helper file, and nothing new for `install-ops.sh` to deploy. This replaces the two copies of `epoch-millis.sh` from the earlier revision.
- The readiness waiter rejects a `completion_finished_ms` later than now + 1 s, so a probe host that still produces nanosecond receipts can't pass for fresh.
- The public health schema checks in `verify-public-homepage.sh` and `capture-gateway-observability.sh` bound `latency_ms` to `[0, 60000]` and require a 13-digit `completion_finished_ms` when it isn't zero.

`devnet/node_scripts/find_best_rpc.sh` also uses `%3N` but belongs to a different tree, so it is left unchanged here.

## Tests

- `scripts/test-gateway-health-probe.sh` runs the real probe with a `date` on `PATH` that behaves like uutils 0.7/0.8, and asserts `latency_ms` is in `[0, 60000]` and `completion_finished_ms` has 13 digits. It fails against the `main` probe and passes on this branch.
- `scripts/test-public-traffic-readiness.sh` adds a nanosecond-scale future receipt, which must be rejected.
- `scripts/test-profiles.sh` fails if any `$(date …%3N)` comes back into `04-ops/` or `scripts/`.
- Locally, `make shellcheck` (ShellCheck v0.11.0) passes, and `GONKA_UPSTREAM_WORKTREE=<gonka clone> make test` passes except `test-recovery-contract`, which was skipped. In this environment it fails the same four assertions (`new persistent output accepted` and three that follow from it) on unmodified `main`.
- CI for this fork PR still needs maintainer approval.

## Deployment status

Nothing is deployed by this PR. The live probe keeps reporting nanosecond latencies until an owner-authorized OPS reinstall puts the updated `gateway-health-probe.sh` on the gateway Host.
